A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ORCA research. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial layout changes and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original imitation-learning results on DeepMind Control, MetaWorld and Adroit, with component, layer and timestep ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds fine-tuning comparisons, LIBERO-Long experiments, alternative-backbone evaluations and visual-encoder ablations.

M1.justification: ORCA retains frozen Stable Diffusion 1.5, learnable task prompts, dense visual prompts and behavior-cloning training. Sections 5–6 preserve the conditioning procedure and default components. The additional backbone and encoder experiments do not establish a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: The original 12 tasks across three suites remain. v2 Appendix A.2 adds KITCHEN-3, LIVING-1 and STUDY-1 from LIBERO-Long, extending evaluation to long-horizon, language-conditioned manipulation and joint multi-task control.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds fully fine-tuned VC-1 and SCR, VC-1 with RoboAdapter, and SCR with LoRA. Appendix Tables A and E add SVD, Stable Diffusion 3.0, standalone DINOv2, SigLIP and Theia comparisons. The original benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce full versus parameter-efficient adaptation, alternative backbone feature-extraction settings, SVD restricted to three input frames, and joint training of three LIBERO tasks with a shared policy. The original demonstration counts, 100-epoch training budget and evaluation every 10 epochs remain unchanged; several added experiments have limited protocol detail.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses testing prompting against downstream fine-tuning, sensitivity to diffusion architecture, and dependence on the visual-prompt encoder, including an SD-VAE alternative without an external encoder. Existing component, layer, attention and qualitative studies remain; the timestep study receives a revised default-result row.

E5.justification: Retained experiments continue reporting means and standard deviations over three seeds. Additional comparisons largely use the same reporting practice, without new significance tests, confidence intervals or an explicit change in repeated-run counts. Updated standard-deviation values belong to the changed results.

E6.justification: The original main benchmark scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results in Table 3 and Appendix Tables A–C and E. For example, ORCA's new LIBERO single-task and multi-task means are 65.5 and 46.6. The default timestep row changes from mean 70.8 to 74.3, including Reacher-easy changing from 71.9 to 87.6, now matching the main results.

T1.justification: The diffusion equations, feature-extraction formulation and behavior-cloning objective remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version contains additional propositions, proofs or formal derivations that alter the theoretical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: textual conditioning can fail in robotic control, learned task and visual prompts enable adaptation without fine-tuning the diffusion model, and ORCA achieves state-of-the-art benchmark performance. Added experiments support these claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of adaptation costs and overfitting, possible SVD failure from input-length mismatch, multi-task applicability, and architecture-specific limitations in Appendix C. It also distinguishes specialist agents from generalist VLAs. However, the retained claim that larger timesteps benefit Reacher-easy contradicts the revised Table D.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link, parameter counts for adaptation baselines, and frame/layer choices for added backbone experiments. It also explicitly describes TADP's single fixed-image conditioning. Existing compression-layer pseudocode and principal hyperparameters remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish availability of downloadable code or data.

R1.justification: v2 substantially broadens positioning beyond frozen encoders and perception-oriented prompting to parameter-efficient adaptation, newer visual encoders, video/Transformer diffusion and VLAs. Corresponding references are added, and Appendix A.8 explicitly contrasts ORCA's specialist focus and image-text pretraining with generalist models trained on robot interaction data.

P1.justification: Most original prose and the main section sequence remain intact. v2 locally revises the abstract and introduction, expands baseline explanations, reorders analyses and moves references after the supplementary material. Section 6.5 also repeats the task/visual-prompt visualization discussion almost verbatim.

P2.justification: v2 converts the document to two columns, moves Figure 1 onto the title page, merges the DMC and MetaWorld tables, and rearranges Figure 6 into a vertical frame sequence. It adds five experimental tables and extensively resizes or relocates retained displays. The appendix rollout visualizations retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the empirical case for conditioning: fine-tuning controls and encoder ablations address alternatives insufficiently tested in v1, while LIBERO experiments broaden validation beyond the original suites. Explicit architecture limitations also improve calibration. Sparse settings for some added experiments, duplicated prose and the stale timestep interpretation temper these gains, but do not outweigh the stronger evidence supporting the method.
